final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor mainly reframed the same record in a narrower and more accurate way. That reframing is useful, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. The distinction matters: a caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is already implemented or otherwise satisfied in the evidentiary record. Here, the record still shows an unresolved material limitation in a named launch use case, a model-card draft that does not disclose it, and no approved mitigation or risk acceptance meeting policy requirements. On that basis, certification may be plausible in principle if disclosure or approved acceptance is completed before launch, but current compliance is not evidenced. The appropriate final assessment remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats or compliant.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows a material weakness in a named launch use case: insurance claims triage remains below target.
The current model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations, so the required disclosure is not evidenced as already made.
No approved mitigation or risk acceptance is in the record with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The draft runbook remains incomplete because accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
Monitoring and public guidance support a possible path to conditional certification, but they do not satisfy the current internal policy predicates on this record.
